# SIM-RUST-v1: a Rust simulator on worlds generated by real Minecraft (design 2026-11-02, first implementation 2026-11-03)

Owner brief 2026-11-02: training on Forge servers is too slow for architecture trials. Generate worlds in normal Minecraft, convert
them to matrices, and implement the behaviour in Rust on the CPU; vanilla first, mods afterwards in a LoRA-like way. **Section 9 records what was built on
2026-11-03 (owner: "implement everything up through the simulator"); sections 1-8 are the design it follows.** Numbers marked (est.) are
estimates, not measurements.

## 1. Why this is smaller than "port Minecraft"

Two facts from this repo cut the port down:

1. **World generation is not ported.** The real server generates the terrain once; the simulator only reads it. The exact worldgen
   (noise router, caves, aquifers, features, structures) never has to be reproduced. Existing worlds already hold it: each training
   world's `region/` is about 387 MB for ~180 region files (measured 2026-11-02, `forgeaip-world_train-data`), and the start sites
   are pre-generated +-176 blocks by design (TASK-20261102-028).
2. **The policy does not act per tick.** One RL step is one command of the action layer (`move_to`, `mine`, `tunnel`, `attack`,
   `craft`, `place`, `smelt`, `eat`, `wait`, `pickup`, 1 tick to 60 s; ~45 ticks median). A simulator that implements the *commands*
   as semi-Markov transitions (outcome, reason, ticks elapsed, inventory and position change) needs no per-tick player physics.
   Ticks matter only for the world clocks that run in between (day/night, hunger, mobs, fluids, crops), and those can advance in
   coarse sub-steps (5 or 20 ticks) while a command is "executing".

So the simulator is: **voxel matrices + a skill-outcome model + coarse world clocks**, validated against the real server.

## 2. World matrices (offline, once)

| Item | Design |
|---|---|
| Source | The server's own `region/*.mca` (Anvil). A converter in Rust (`tools/world-export`, `fastnbt` + `flate2`) reads chunk NBT. |
| Per chunk | `blocks`: 24 sections x 4096 x `u16` vanilla block-state id (state ids are unchanged on Forge; `modpack/forgeaip-create.registry.json` maps names and states); `biome`: 6x6x(384/4) `u8` per chunk; `height`: motion-blocking heightmap `u16` 16x16; light is recomputed. |
| Storage | One tile file per site: 23 x 23 chunks around a start site (the pregen area), palette-compressed sections, zstd. (est.) 8-15 MB per tile, 2,000 tiles = 16-30 GB on `/mnt/data`; the chunk store is memory-mapped. |
| Raw size in RAM | 98,304 blocks x 2 B = 192 KB per chunk (dense); a 23 x 23 tile = 100 MB dense, so the simulator loads only +-6 chunks around a bot and pages the rest. 20 worlds x 2 bots stay near 1 GB (est.), under today's ~1.2 GB for **one** Forge server. |
| Outside the tile | Hard boundary (the command fails `unreachable`, as an unloaded chunk would). How far bots really get from their site in an episode is **not measured yet**; phase 1 measures the maximum distance from the per-step positions in the run logs before the tile size is fixed. |
| Entities | Not stored. Mobs spawn in the simulator by rule (section 3). Block entities (chests, furnaces) are created empty. Villages and other structures come along as blocks. |
| Reuse | A tile is read-only; an episode copies the touched chunks (copy-on-write) and drops them at the end, so one tile serves unlimited episodes with different seeds for mobs, weather and time. |

## 3. What has to be implemented (vanilla), and how faithfully

Fidelity target: **the distribution of (success, reason, dt, deltas) of each command matches the real action layer**, not tick-exact
Minecraft. Oracle for each row: the Forge test server and the existing benches.

| Part | Approach | Oracle / test |
|---|---|---|
| Voxel store, state tables | Block properties (hardness, tool, drops, shape class, light, fluid) from the vanilla data-generator reports (extracted from the server jar by running `--reports`); no hand-typed tables. | Count of mismatches vs `registry.json` = 0. |
| Reachability and `move_to` | A* / flood fill on the walker's own move set (walk, step, drop, swim, ladder; port of `src/skills/planner` rules, they are already data-like). Duration = path length / measured speeds (walk 4.3, sprint, swim, ladder blocks/s) + start-up ticks. | `tests/test_skills_motion_sim.js` (prismarine-physics) as ground truth; bench scenarios (17 x 5). |
| `mine` / `tunnel` | Break time = vanilla formula (hardness, tool tier and speed, enchant-free, on-ground, in-water), drops from loot tables (generator report), gravity blocks (sand, gravel) fall, fluids released. | Bench rates in SKILLS-v1 (560/560 flat, 0.93 natural); drops vs server statistics. |
| `craft` / `smelt` | Recipes straight from the vanilla recipe JSONs (generator report); smelt times and fuel values from the tables. | Recipe book of the real server, all recipes. |
| `place`, `equip`, `eat`, `activate` | Rule sets (placement support, tool durability, food values). | Unit tests against server behaviour. |
| Time, weather, light | Tick counter, day/night, light levels from block light + sky light (recompute per touched chunk), sleeping skips the night. | `time query`, dawn events in the logs. |
| Hunger, health, damage, death | Vanilla formulas (exhaustion, saturation, regen, fall damage, drowning, lava, starvation); death respawns at the site with an empty inventory (reward v6). | Statistics deltas. |
| Fluids | Water and lava spread (level rules, source blocks) on touched columns only, in 5-tick sub-steps; no redstone, no pistons. | Bench scenarios with water; swim tests. |
| Mobs | A small set first: zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider, cow, pig, sheep, chicken (spawn rules by light and biome, simple approach / flee / attack, damage tables). Pathing = the same A* on the voxels. | Kill and damage statistics from the training logs (`killed`, `deaths`); calibrate, do not claim equivalence. |
| Not simulated | Redstone, pistons, farming growth beyond crops-as-blocks, villagers, trading, enchanting, brewing, Nether and End logic (separate later phase), most structures' loot. | Documented gaps; candidates for them are not offered. |

The progress list (24 entries up to `craft_diamond_pickaxe`) needs only: wood, planks, table, sticks, wooden and stone tools, furnace,
coal, torch, food, a hostile kill, iron, smelting, bed and sleep, diamond. Everything above in the table is that list's closure; the
rest can wait.

## 4. Interface: the learner must not change

The simulator speaks the **same file API** the environment speaks today (`integrations/botsystem`: `hello`, `obs`, `act`, JSONL per
run, DPOD `botsystem_goal_ppo.py` on the other end), one process per group of 2, built as `tools/sim` (Rust, std + a few crates).
`candidates()` of `src/rl/skill_space.js` (K = 64, reachability, quotas, `feat`) is ported 1:1; its output is the contract. A later
step replaces the files by shared memory or a batched in-process call (PyO3) because file polling would otherwise cap the rate.

## 5. Cost (est.)

| Quantity | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Per step in the simulator | 0.05 - 0.5 ms for most commands; A* with a node cap ~0.2 - 1 ms; observation + candidates ~0.3 ms. So **1,000 - 3,000 steps/s per core**, 6 - 18k/s on 6 cores. Real Forge today: 13.5 steps/s for 20 bots. |
| The consequence | **The learner becomes the limit**: ~20 steps/s on the PC CPU in run 7 (458 steps per 22 s update). The GPU learner (3060 Ti) must go from 20 to at least several hundred steps/s for the simulator to matter; the simulator's rate is capped by the learner, not the other way round. A learner benchmark on the GPU comes **before** any simulator work. |
| Code | Scoped simulator 12-18k lines of Rust, mostly tables read from generator reports and the ported planner; world exporter ~1k; differential test harness ~1.5k. 6-10 weeks (est.). Full tick-level port: 35-60k lines, many person-months; not recommended. |
| Risk | The policy exploits simulator gaps (a command that is too easy or never fails). Mitigation: a fixed real-server evaluation arm (the existing bench plus an episode eval on a Forge test copy) every N updates; promotion only on that arm. |

## 6. Mod stage ("LoRA-like")

1. **Vocabulary**: the id embedding tables (items, blocks, entities) are created with spare rows now; mod ids are new rows (trained),
   vanilla rows frozen. `hello.vocab` already carries id -> name per run.
2. **Adapters**: low-rank adapters (rank 4-8) on the attention and candidate heads, trained while the base is frozen; a gated
   residual so the vanilla behaviour is unchanged when the adapter is off.
3. **Where**: on the real Forge server (Create etc. cannot be simulated cheaply), starting from the vanilla-trained policy. Far fewer
   steps are needed than from scratch; the throughput of today's setup is enough if the base is good.
4. Open: whether mod blocks can be given a coarse class (solid, fluid, machine) so the simulator can run some of this stage too.

## 7. Phases

0. **Measure the learner** (GPU vs CPU, steps/s at batch sizes); decides whether anything below pays off.
1. Exporter + one tile per training world; loader and a viewer that checks the matrices against `bot.blockAt` on the live server (0 mismatches).
2. Movement and mining skills + candidate generation; differential bench against the 17 scenarios; accept at <= 2 pp success difference per command and a dt ratio within 15 %.
3. Crafting, smelting, placing, time, hunger, death; the progress-list episode end to end vs a real episode of the scripted teacher (same commands, compare the item and time trajectory).
4. Mobs and combat; calibrate against the logs.
5. Training on the simulator, evaluation on the real server arm.

## 8. Decisions needed from the owner

- Skill-level semi-Markov simulation (recommended, section 1) or tick-level. The brief reads like tick-level; tick-level costs 3-5x the code and a 10-50x lower step rate for the same machine.
- Tile size (+-176 as pregenerated now, or larger) and how many sites (2,000 = 16-30 GB est.).
- Whether Nether and End are in scope for the first version (the progress list stops before them).
- Licensing line: world files and generator reports are data from the owner's own server; no decompiled Mojang code is copied into the simulator.

## 9. Implemented 2026-11-03 (`tools/sim`, Rust, std only, no dependencies)

| Part | State |
|---|---|
| `gen_data.js` | Data tables from the same minecraft-data 1.20.1 and registry the real environment uses: 1,003 blocks (hardness, tool multipliers, harvest tools, drops, kind, observation category), 2,409 recipes (table or not), foods, and the **identical** item (1,955) and entity (125) vocabularies. |
| `forgeaip-sim export` | Anvil reader (own zlib/NBT, no crates) -> tiles of 15 x 15 chunks around each site candidate, written only if every chunk is `minecraft:full`. Run on the five training worlds: **98 tiles, 833 MB** (`/mnt/data/forgeaip/sim-tiles`, 8-10 MB each). Mod blocks (Create ores and stones) become `stone`; block states are dropped (ids only). |
| `forgeaip-sim run` | The environment side of the file API (hello / obs / act, same fields, reward v6 terms, progress list judged from events, episodes of N days, respawn with an empty inventory, trapped-bot kill, new tile and start site per episode with the 12-logs and dry-ground checks). One process per shard (group); bots in their own tiles. |
| Skills | `move_to` (flood fill on the walker's own move set, Dijkstra, 1,500 nodes, radius 18), `mine` (vanilla break time from hardness and tool multiplier, drops, gravity blocks, liquid inflow, line of sight), `tunnel`, `craft` (all recipes, 2x2 or table), `smelt` (fuel), `place`, `eat`, `attack` (zombies and four passive mobs, drops, kill stats), `activate` (bed: sleep skips the night), `wait`. |
| Candidates / observation | Port of `skill_space.js`: K = 64, quotas, move headings, mine per type nearest + head height, tunnel steps, attack, craft, smelt, place, eat, wait; grid 9x9x5, view rays 16x8 with first-hit category / item / distance, entities, inventory, self. |
| World clocks | Time of day, dawn and sleeping, hunger and regeneration, zombie spawning at night and underground, daylight burn-off. |
| Learner | DPOD `botsystem_goal_ppo.py` unchanged in its interface; new `--max-queue` (backpressure: observations wait in the files while the learner is behind) and `--max-steps` (final checkpoint, `exchange/<base>.done`, the shards exit). |

**Measured** (smoke test `tools/sim/tests/smoke_policy.py`, one shard, a Python policy over the files, 40 s): 361 steps/s through the
file API (the Python policy is the limit, not the simulator); the scripted teacher reaches 11-16 of 24 progress entries per
3-day episode; 98-100 % of mine / move / craft / place / smelt succeed, `tunnel` 99 % (stuck 44 of 3,825), 6 of ~14,400
steps ended in death. Real Forge runs reached 8 of 24 without a teacher, so these numbers say the simulator is *playable*, not
that it is *faithful*.

**Not done / known gaps** (as of 2026-11-03 morning; section 11 removes several of them and lists what remains):
- No differential test against the Forge server yet (phase 2 of section 7): break times, walking speed (4.317 b/s), fight
  length, mob damage and spawn rates are formula- or estimate-based; commands never fail at random, whereas the real action
  layer fails ~2-6 % of the time (`stuck`, `not_confirmed`).
- Block ids only: no water levels, no waterlogging, no doors or beds as two-block states; fluids do not spread.
- Mobs: zombies and four passive animals, no pathfinding beyond a greedy step, no skeletons, creepers or spiders; no fall damage
  (the walker never drops more than 3 blocks); no natural stations or beds (placed ones only).
- Tiles end 112 blocks from the site; past the edge a command fails `unreachable`. How far real bots get is still unmeasured.
- Statistics `picked_up` are emitted at the moment a drop is added (no item entities).
- The live board (`train-dash`) shows nothing for simulator runs; `scripts/train/sim.sh status` and the learner log are the views.

## 10. Validation against the Forge server (2026-11-03)

Setup (`scripts/train/validate-sim.sh`, `tools/sim/compare.py`): the same stand-in policy (the DPOD scripted teacher on the progress
list, `tools/sim/tests/smoke_policy.py`), the same two worlds (volumes `train-data`, `train-data-s1`), the same 14 start sites (tiles
and `exchange/sites-val.json`), 2 bots per world, 3-day episodes, reward v6. Real: two Forge 1.20.1 servers at speed 2, 70 min,
**19,302 steps, 8 finished episodes**. Simulator: 14 min, **551,411 steps, 265 finished episodes**.

| Measure | Real Forge | Simulator | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `move_to`: success / median ticks | 0.99 / 54 | 0.99 / 55 | agrees |
| `wait` 40, `smelt` ~205, `eat` ~33, `attack` ~240 ticks | 40 / 208 / 35.5 / 241 | 40 / 202 / 32 / 236 | agrees |
| `tunnel`: success / median ticks | 0.96 / 70 | 0.99 / 42 | success close, 40 % too fast |
| `mine`: success / median ticks | 0.79 / 76 | 1.00 / 27 | 2.8x too fast, never fails |
| `craft`: median ticks | 1 | 5 | too slow by the walk constant |
| `place`: success | **0.22** | 1.00 | does not agree (see below) |
| `craft` at a placed table | mostly `unreachable` (about 600 of ~800) | `no_station` or ok | different failure |
| `attack` success | 0.35 | 0.94 | too easy |
| Steps per finished episode | 2,036 | 2,063 | agrees (the policy's loops cost the same) |
| Progress entries at 1/3 / 2/3 / end | 8.6 / 10.9 / **12.0** (range 8-14) | 12.3 / 13.8 / **14.2** | same shape, simulator 18-40 % ahead |
| Deaths per 3-day episode | **20.6** (5-39) | **4.3** | 5x too safe |
| Survival reward (days lived of 3) | 0.25 | 1.51 | too safe |

Reading: the **order of magnitude and the shape of progress agree**, and the movement and fixed-duration commands agree closely,
but the simulator is **too lenient**: it is faster at mining and tunnelling, never fails a placement, fights too easily and, above
all, is five times too safe. Run `sim1`'s numbers (progress 14, deaths 0.9 per episode) must therefore not be read as real-game
performance; the real game at the same policy gives about 12 entries and about 20 deaths.

What the real logs show (events.jsonl of the real run): the teacher gets into a loop of 1,139 successful and 3,716 `invalid_target`
placements of crafting tables, followed by 3x3 crafts at the placed table that fail `unreachable` (`stone_pickaxe`, `stone_sword`,
`furnace`, ~197 each). That is a real-game behaviour of the action layer (a placed table is often not a reachable station) that the
simulator does not have. It is also the single biggest source of `invalid` reward in the real run (-210 in one episode).

Calibration targets, in order of effect (each needs a re-run of this comparison to confirm):
1. Hostile pressure: skeletons, spiders, creepers, more zombies, arrows; target 15-25 deaths per episode for the teacher.
2. Station reach and placement: placed tables are often unreachable and `place` often invalid; find the action layer's rule in
   `src/skills/commands` (candidate spot vs the command's own goal) and port it instead of fitting noise.
3. `mine` / `tunnel` time: add the approach and aim overhead (real median 76 and 70 ticks); `craft` 1 tick; random `stuck`,
   `not_confirmed`, `cancelled` at the real rates (2-6 %).
4. Combat: `attack` success 0.35 with cancellations and `target_lost`.

Not tested: the *learned* policy of `sim1` in the real game (the checkpoint is kept in `/mnt/data/forgeaip/sim1-final-checkpoint-910k.pkl`;
`--init` on a `--learn 0` run of the real environment is the test).

## 11. Why it was too safe and too lenient: causes measured on the real server (2026-11-03)

Owner brief 2026-11-03: "too safe: separate the causes (spawn rate? knockback or being trapped? damage calculation?); placement and
destruction succeed too often, the real line of sight is blocked or the view is shifted by attacks; the learning status is unknown;
no stopgaps, find the root causes". Section 10 compared rates. This section compares **causes**, and changes the simulator only
where a cause is a rule of the game or of the action layer, never to fit a rate.

### 11.1 Method

- The real environment now logs, per command, what hurt the bot (`damage_event` of the server: damage type and attacker, amount
  from the next health packet; `death_combat_event`: the death message; `src/rl/damage_log.js`), why a command failed (the
  `SkillError` detail and the phases it went through) and where the ticks went (`ph`); env `2026-11-03-skills-v3.2`.
- Two real runs of the same stand-in policy (the scripted teacher), same worlds and sites: **A** (section 10; 19,302 steps, 8.71
  bot-hours = 8.7 three-day episodes of game time, no cause log) and **B** (this session; 6,808 steps, 4.76 bot-hours, with the cause log).
- The simulator writes the same `events.jsonl` rows; `tools/sim/causes.py` tabulates damage by cause, exposure (observations with
  a hostile within 16 blocks, by kind and distance) and failures by command, real and sim side by side.

### 11.2 The target is heavy-tailed: one real run is not a number

Deaths per bot-hour (= per 3-day episode): run A **22.2** (193 deaths), run B **4.0** (19 deaths; 6 of them the environment's own
stuck kills). Poisson intervals do not overlap (A 19-26, B 2.4-6.2). Section 10's "five times too safe" compared the simulator with
run A alone. The honest target is the pooled rate, **15.7** per bot-hour (212 deaths in 13.5 bot-hours), with the knowledge that a
single run can land anywhere between 4 and 22. Hit points lost per bot-hour: A about 223 (attributed to the nearest hostile in
the observation stream), B 97.

### 11.3 Cause 1 of "too safe": it was not the spawn rate and not the zombie damage

From run A's observations (nearest hostile within 16 blocks, hit points lost between consecutive observations, per game minute):

| | real | simulator before |
|---|---:|---:|
| bot with a zombie within 2 blocks (share of observations) | 1.2 % | 1.2 % |
| hostile of any kind within 16 blocks, day / night | 4.7 % / 17.4 % | 25.0 % / 28.5 % |
| hp lost per minute with a zombie within 2 blocks | 72 | 66 |
| P(any loss in that interval) | 0.60 | 0.62 |
| hp lost per minute with a zombie 2-4 blocks away | 20.5 | 4.4 |

Contact with zombies and the damage of a zombie in contact agreed; the simulator had more hostile presence than the game, not less.
What differed: **(a) kinds**: real hp loss by nearest hostile kind was zombie 52 %, skeleton 22 %, drowned 7 %, creeper 5 %, spider
4.5 %, enderman 2 %, nothing in view 7 %; the simulator had zombies only. In run B (damage events): arrows 39 %, drowning 31 %,
zombie melee 14 %, creeper 7 %, fall 4 %, spider 3 %, starvation 2 % of the attributed hit points. **(b) the zone just outside
contact**: arrows land at 4-8 blocks (24-44 hp/min), a zombie that has just been knocked back or is closing in still hits.
Deaths grow faster than damage (a death needs 20 hp inside the regeneration window), so 0.42x of the damage gave about 0.2x of the deaths.

**Knockback and trapping**: knockback was absent but cannot be the main cause, since damage in contact already matched without
it. Trapping was present in the real game and absent in the simulator, for a reason outside combat (11.4).

### 11.4 Cause 2: placement and mining fail by the action layer's rules, and the policy repeats the failure

Run B, failures of the commands that matter, counted as failures and as distinct (bot, episode, target):

| command and reason | failures | distinct targets | what it is |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| place `unreachable` | 401 | 5 (181 on one) | one bot sealed in a one-block pit: crafting tables W and N, soil E and S, a leaf canopy two blocks above the rim; the planner expanded 1 node, no placement face is visible from inside the column |
| place `invalid_target` | 338 | 5 | `cell holds torch` (and similar): the candidate list treats a torch as free air, `place` accepts only REPLACEABLE blocks |
| mine `unreachable` | 255 | 10 (198 on one) | the planner searched 20,000 nodes and found no stand cell with an aim point: geometry allows the aim from the candidate's node, but the command's re-approach (reach 3.3) probably has none (not verified); the new `entity_in_the_way` marker in the next real run will say whether a mob or a dropped item stands on every ray |

So the high failure rates are a few degenerate states counted hundreds of times, each created by a **mismatch between what the candidate
list offers and what the command requires**, and kept alive by a policy that repeats the same command. "The view was shifted by a
monster attack" is not supported by the data: of 2,921 `mine` and `place` commands in run B, 23 (0.8 %) took any damage; 4 of the 5
failures among the 17 damaged `mine` commands were deaths (`cancelled`), the `place` ones succeeded 3 of 6; none of the 401 + 338 + 255
failures of the table happened in a command that took damage. Knockback may matter in other states; here it cannot explain more
than a percent of the failures.

The simulator accepted any air cell with a floor, regardless of the cell's block, of placement faces, and of whether anyone could
stand where a face is visible, so none of these states could exist.

### 11.5 What changed in the simulator (each item a rule, with its source)

1. Aim points and reach goals ported from `geometry.js aimPoints` / `motion.js reachGoal`: `mine`, `place`, `craft` at a table, `smelt`,
   sleeping need a stand cell reachable on the walker's graph with a visible aim point (face centre and four inner points, faces turned
   away skipped); the candidate list uses the same predicate for `mine` as `skill_space.js minable`.
2. `place`: target must be REPLACEABLE (`block.js`), needs a solid neighbour and a stand cell outside the target's column from which an
   aim point on that neighbour's face toward the target is visible; a mob in the cell makes it `not_confirmed`. Unit test: the 9x5x9
   block categories of the recorded trap rebuild the pit, and `place` ends `unreachable`, as in the game; the same cell with a sapling
   ends `invalid_target`.
3. Mobs by the game's rules (`tools/sim/src/mobs.rs`): zombie (reach 1.9, 3 hp, 1 s), skeleton (arrows need a line of sight, 15
   blocks, one per 2.5 s, hit chance falls with distance), creeper (fuse 1.5 s inside 3 blocks, cancelled beyond 7, damage
   floor((i^2+i)/2 x 42 + 1) with i = (1 - distance/6) x exposure), spider (neutral by day); melee knockback shoves the bot; mobs
   chase down the walker's own distance field (round walls, up one block); despawn 2.5 % per second beyond 32 blocks. Fights run through
   the world clock; a death in a command ends it `cancelled` (what the real runner reports).
4. Hunger as in the game: no passive drain (it was 0.57 food per 1,000 ticks, real 0.25), exhaustion from actions, saturation,
   healing 6 exhaustion per hp, fast healing while food is full; drowning (15 s of air, then 2 hp per second); darkness from opaque
   blocks overhead (leaves do not count: under a canopy the old rule spawned monsters in daylight).
5. **Fitted, and only these**: `SPAWN_NIGHT` 0.05 and `SPAWN_DARK` 0.07 attempts per second, the spawn weights per kind (zombie 1.4,
   skeleton 3.0, creeper 1.4, spider 0.4) and the exhaustion per walked block 0.02: set so that the share of observations with a
   hostile within 16 blocks, by kind and distance, and the food loss per tick match the real server (run A + B pooled). The game's own
   spawn algorithm (light levels, 70-mob cap, pack sizes, biome lists) is not reproduced.

### 11.6 Result (same stand-in policy, same 14 sites; simulator 14 min = 405,496 steps = 217 bot-hours = 216 finished episodes)

| Measure | real A | real B | simulator before | simulator now |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `place` success | 0.22 | 0.46 | 1.00 | **0.35** |
| `place` failures: `unreachable` / `invalid_target` | 19 % / 53 % | 29 % / 24 % | 0 | 45 % / 17 % |
| `craft` median ticks / success | 1 / 0.82 | 2 / 0.98 | 5 / - | **1 / 0.85** |
| `mine` success | 0.79 | 0.82 | 1.00 | 0.99 |
| `mine` median ticks | 76 | 72 | 27 | 51 |
| `tunnel` median ticks | 70 | 71 | 42 | 84 |
| `attack` success | 0.35 | 0.53 (n = 17) | 0.94 | 0.80 |
| steps per finished episode | 2,036 | 1,287 | 2,063 | **1,867** |
| progress entries at the end of an episode | 12.0 | 11.75 | 14.2 | **12.95** |
| progress at 1/3 of the run | 8.6 | 10.75 | 12.3 | 10.2 |
| deaths per finished episode (= per bot-hour) | 20.6 | 4.0 | 4.3 | **9.5** (pooled real 15.7) |
| days survived of 3 (reward) | 0.25 | 1.0 | 1.51 | **0.80** |
| hp lost per bot-hour | ~223 | 97 | ~88 (zombies only) | **206** |
| share of observations with a hostile within 4 blocks | 2.3 % | 0.4 % | 2.8 % | 1.4 % (pooled real 1.8 %) |
| ... within 16 blocks, day / night | 4.7 / 17.4 % | 4.3 / 6.3 % | 25 / 29 % | 5.6 / 26 % (pooled real 4.6 / 14.5 %) |
| food lost per 1,000 ticks | | 0.25 | 0.57 | 0.35 |

The pooled real deaths (15.7 per bot-hour) lie between the two real runs (22.2 and 4.0); the simulator's 9.5 lies between them too, and
the progress, survival and return of the simulator are now inside the range of the two real runs where before they were outside it on
every line. Rates that were wrong by construction (`place` 1.00, `craft` 5 ticks, zombie-only damage) are no longer wrong; rates that
depend on the real server's heavy tail (deaths, return) can only be matched in range with two real runs.

### 11.7 What is still different (do not read simulator numbers past this list)

1. **`mine` never fails** in the simulator (0.99) and fails 17-18 % in the game (`unreachable`, 255 failures from 10 targets): the
   cause is not geometry (the candidate list and the command use the same predicate) but something the simulator does not have, most
   likely an entity on every ray (a dropped item, a mob) or the second approach with the smaller reach; the next real run logs
   `entity_in_the_way` and the phase ticks and will say which. Until then the simulator is too kind to the policy exactly where the
   real policy loses most `invalid` reward.
2. **Timing of `mine` / `tunnel`** (51 vs 72-76 and 84 vs 70 ticks) comes from three constants estimated from the command's own waits
   (`MINE_HOLD`, `MINE_AIM`, `MINE_COLLECT`); the per-phase ticks of the next real run replace them.
3. **Combat**: `attack` succeeds 0.80 against 0.35-0.53; the simulator fights deterministically at 12 ticks per swing without
   cooldown misses, retreats, or the mob walking away (`target_lost`, `stuck`).
4. **Lethality by kind**: zombie melee 101 hp/h against 10 (B) and about 117 (A, by attribution), creepers 45 against 5 (B) and
   about 11 (A), drowning 3.5 against 23 (B) and 7 % of A's loss: the simulator has no swimming through deep water and floods only
   one cell, and falls are not modelled (4 % in B). Starvation is now 0 (real 1.5 hp/h) and food loss 0.35 against 0.25 per 1,000 ticks. Hostile presence at night is 26 % against
   14.5 % pooled and within 16 blocks overall 8.6 % against 5.0 %, skeletons (7.6 %) hover at the distance the model gives them
   (8 blocks) where the real ones are seen 3.3 % of the time. Contact (within 2 blocks) matches.
5. **Mobs**: no endermen, witches, drowned, husks, slimes, phantoms, no pack spawns, no armour, no light levels from torches;
   hostile mobs never leave the tile edge's 112 blocks.
6. Section 9's other gaps (block ids only, no fluids spreading, no natural stations or beds, drops without item entities) stand.

### 11.8 What this means for the next training run

The verdict `stalled` of run sim1 (TRAIN-STATUS-v1) was reached on a simulator that let the policy place, craft and survive more than the
game does; it does not say what the policy would do in the game, and it does not say the design is wrong. A run on the corrected
simulator can be judged with the same rule. Open items before trusting a simulator number as a game number: the list above, one real
run with the new logging (`ph`, `entity_in_the_way`), and the sim1 checkpoint played in the real game with `--learn 0`.

## 12. Follow-up (2026-11-04): why `mine` never failed, and the alignment of ticks, damage and enemy counts

Owner: "that mining does not fail cannot be left alone; estimate the cause from the logs (most likely designated blocks that cannot be reached, which the simulator destroys anyway); align ticks, damage and enemy counts". A third real run (C, 60 min, 20,451 steps, with per-phase ticks) and the PC's GPU made this possible; the pooled real data is now 12.2 bot-hours with the cause log and 21 with observations.

### 12.1 Mining: confirmed, reproduced, ported

- **Real log**, first half of run C: 1,202 of 1,979 `mine` commands failed `unreachable`, from **5 distinct targets** (one repeated 1,001 times), all 2-6 blocks above the feet; run B: 255 from 10 targets. None of them carries the `entity_in_the_way` marker, so a mob or an item on the line of sight is ruled out; the targets are not at the reach limit (nearest point 1.4-2.8 blocks).
- **Mechanism, reproduced offline with the real code**: `tests/case_mine_canopy.json` is the saved world around the 198-times target of run B (a floating log inside a leaf canopy). Replayed with the real `planner.js` / `motion.js reachGoal` / `geometry.js aimPoints`: the candidate test of `skill_space.js` passes with **one** stand cell, (3242,86,1256), and **one** aim point through a gap in the leaves; the command walks there, but the body stops up to 0.25 off the cell centre, and from 2 of the 4 offsets tried the aim point is gone (`visible()` false); the second attempt (reach 3.3, another cell) has no goal in the whole search (`expanded` 20,000), so the command ends `unreachable` and the bot ends back where it started. The policy offers the same candidate again, every time. This is the owner's hypothesis, with the exact reason: the block is designated through a sight line that the body cannot hold, and the simulator, standing exactly at the cell centre, destroyed it.
- **Ported** (`Sim::approach`, `motion.js approachUntil`): attempt 0 to the cheapest goal cell (reach 4.1), look from where the body really stopped (an offset up to 0.25, a fixed function of start and cell: the same walk gives the same stop, which is why the real failure repeats 198 times), then attempt 1 with reach 3.3 and another cell; the bot returns to its start when the second plan fails. Unit test: the recorded case ends `unreachable` twice, with the bot back at its start. It is used by `mine`, `place`, `craft` at a table, `smelt` and sleeping.
- **Result** (PC validation vs real B + C): `mine` `unreachable` 0.45 against 0.35 (+ `not_visible` 0.03); never-mined targets (first PC validation, before the final constants) 0.34 % of distinct targets in the simulator against 0.64 % in the game; failures per such target up to 1,450 against 1,003. The failing heights are the canopy (+4) in the simulator and +2/+4 in the game.

### 12.2 Tick times, from the per-phase record (`ph`, tools/sim/phases.py, ticks.py)

Real per-phase means (1,984 `mine`, 793 `tunnel`, 851 `move_to`): a walk costs 24.0 + 5.69 ticks per block (the idealised 4.63 plus a settle); `mine` = approach walk 6.3 + dig phase 45.6 + collect_drop 20.0 + the walk to a drop that did not land at the feet 18.3; a tunnel step ends with a 39-tick walk-in. The simulator's constants (`ticks_for` x1.06 + 5, `MINE_CONFIRM` 6, `MINE_COLLECT` 20, `MINE_PICKUP` 19, `TUNNEL_STEP` 39, first dug cell pays the swap, aim and drop, the next cells 3 + dig) are those numbers, not fits to the totals. Final validation (pooled real runs against 294 bot-hours of the simulator, mean ticks of successful commands): `move_to` 73.4 / 72.0, `place` 8.6 / 8.7, `wait` 40 / 40, `mine` 83.9 / 93.6 (the `ph`-based means 89.2 / 93.6), `smelt` 260 / 224, `eat` 36 / 32; `tunnel` 107 / 132 and `craft` 3.4 / 4.5 before the last change (tunnel step, applied to the simulator after the PC training runs below had started, which therefore ran with the 132); `attack` 277 / 160 (n = 21 real).

### 12.3 Enemy counts and damage

- Mob parameters are physical where the game gives them (zombie reach 2.0 / 3 hp / 1 s, knockback half a block, arrows with line of sight, creeper fuse and falloff, quarter-second steps within 8 blocks of a hostile, chasing down a 6,000-cell path field, despawn beyond 32 blocks, a bot walking away is not hit while it walks, water that flows). Only the arrival rates and kind weights are fitted (`FORGEAIP_MOBS` sweeps on the PC): `SPAWN_NIGHT` 0.015, `SPAWN_DARK` 0.06 per second, weights zombie 1.4, skeleton 3.0, creeper 1.4, spider 0.4.
- **Enemy counts now match** (share of observations with a hostile within 16 blocks; real pooled A + B + C / simulator): day 4.1 % / 3.7 %, night 14.7 % / 14.6 %, any time 4.8 % / 4.7 %; within 2 blocks 0.9 % / 0.8 %; by kind zombie 3.8 / 4.4, skeleton 3.0 / 3.9, creeper 1.1 / 1.0, spider 0.6 / 0.6 (drowned 0.7, enderman 0.4, witch 0.1: absent).
- **Damage does not match yet, and is not forced to**: hit points per bot-hour, real / simulator: zombie melee 94.6 / 63, arrows 40.0 / 25.5, creeper 7.5 / 16.0, spider 9.5 / 3.6, drowning 27.6 / 2.6, drowned tridents 13.5 / 0, the environment's own stuck kills and unattributed losses 53 / 0, falls 1.6 / 0; deaths per bot-hour 10.6 / 6.6. With the same number of enemies in sight the simulated bot is hit about 0.65 times as often as the real one. A multiplier would hide the cause, so none is applied; candidates not yet separated: how long real mobs stay in contact (their pathing and the bot's stops), the real bot's slower reaction under server lag, and the missing drowned / swimming / fall deaths (together 25 % of the real hit points and 18 % of the real deaths).

### 12.4 Consequence for the training runs

The runs on the PC (below) used the simulator of commit 66fd0171: enemy counts, mining failures, walking and mining ticks as above, damage about 0.65x. They are valid as runs on a world that is somewhat gentler than the game in fights and lacks drowning; a policy that learns to avoid water or fights would be learning a different game on those two points.
